This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT:
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.

IDEA: behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts
TITLE: RQ-VAE residual quantization performed in per-item Poincare charts whose origin is the hyperbolic Frechet mean of the item's training-only successor neighbourhood
MOTIVATION: Content-only SIDs are assigned in one global flat coordinate system, so two items that users actually move between can receive unrelated code prefixes, and the residual chain is a straight Euclidean line that has no reason to follow a behavioural neighbourhood. A generative recommender then wastes prefix capacity on content similarity that does not predict the next item.
NOVELTY: The behaviour signal is not a loss weight, a graph regulariser, a Sinkhorn marginal or a hierarchy constraint. It selects the BASE POINT (gauge) of the curved coordinate system in which every residual is measured and every codeword is decoded, and the residual chain itself advances by geodesic exp maps. The same code tuple therefore means "this geodesic displacement from my own behavioural anchor", which is a different coupling position from behaviour-weighted assignment, curved hierarchy and transition-residual losses: here behaviour enters through log_a / exp_a, i.e. inside the geometric primitive that produces the code.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean residual quantizer of the RQ-VAE by a chart-relative geodesic residual quantizer. Each item's target point p_i is written as log_{a_i}(p_i) at a behaviour-derived anchor a_i, each quantized level moves the reconstruction along a geodesic exp_{p-hat}(q_l), and the next residual is taken at the new point; anchors are refreshed every epoch from a stop-gradient encoder snapshot and the training transition graph.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Poincare ball with fixed curvature c = 1 (radius 1). Encoder z_i in R^d, scale s = median over training items of ||z_i|| measured at Stage-2 epoch 0 and frozen, p_i = exp_0(s * tanh(z_i / s)). Training-only directed successor counts c_ij from Stage-2 sequences give top-K (K = 8) neighbours and weights w_ij proportional to c_ij. Anchor a_i = two-step Karcher mean of {p_j : j in N(i)} under d_Poincare, detached, EMA-smoothed, clamped to radius 0.5 s; a_i = 0 if N(i) is empty. Quantization with L = 3 levels and codebooks C_l of 256 vectors in the tangent frame: r_1 = log_{a_i}(p_i); q_l = argmin_{c in C_l} ||r_l - c||^2; p-hat_0 = a_i; p-hat_l = exp_{p-hat_{l-1}}(q_l); r_{l+1} = log_{p-hat_l}(p_i); SID(i) = (k_1, k_2, k_3). Loss = d_Poincare(p-hat_L, p_i)^2 / s^2 + sum_l ||sg(r_l) - q_l||^2 + 0.25 * sum_l ||r_l - sg(q_l)||^2, with the baseline content decoder fed log_0(p-hat_L). Cost: at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 1023 items/step) each step performs about 1023 * 3 * 3 = 9.2k exp/log calls, roughly 2 MFLOP, plus an anchor refresh of 24556 * 8 * 2 * 2 = 0.8M map calls once per epoch (about 0.1-0.2 s), so total wall clock is at most about 1.05x baseline and memory grows by 24556 * d floats for anchors plus the cached sparse successor graph (tens of MB).'}
COST: <=1.05x baseline wall clock and <=1.1x peak memory; per step at the frozen scale: ~9.2k Poincare exp/log evaluations (~2 MFLOP, vectorised over 1023 items per step), ~0.05 s/step amortised anchor cost (0.1-0.2 s per epoch for all 24556 anchors over 3000 epochs). No extra forward or backward pass through the encoder.
HYPOTHESIS: If behavioural adjacency is better captured by "equal geodesic displacement from a shared anchor" than by "equal absolute position", transition-neighbour items will share first-level codes and longer prefixes more often than in the behaviour-off and geometry-off configurations, the generative model will emit valid prefixes longer, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 with the diagnostics moving in the same direction. Observed by: (i) first-level code agreement rate over training transition pairs, (ii) mean shared prefix length over the same pairs, (iii) code-tuple Jaccard against the both-off reference, (iv) Stage-3 test_recall@10.
RISKS: ['(1) The encoder may collapse all p_i near the origin, making anchors and the origin indistinguishable and degenerating the mechanism into the behaviour-off arm; the EMA plus the 0.5 s clamp does not prevent collapse, only mitigates drift. (2) For long-tail items the successor set is tiny or empty, so their anchors are noisy or zero and their codes behave like the behaviour-off arm. (3) Codebooks shared across heterogeneous tangent frames may mix incomparable directions and hurt more than the anchoring helps. (4) With a geodesic residual the first level already absorbs most of the displacement, so levels 2 and 3 can die, which shortens effective prefixes and can lower recall. (5) A per-epoch anchor refresh creates a moving quantization target that can oscillate.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BRANCHCURV-SID
TITLE: Behaviour-branching curvature field on the RQ-VAE codebook metric
MOTIVATION: Items differ in how predictable their training successors are. Items in a high-fan-out region need coarse cells with fine boundaries, while items on a narrow chain need sharp cells. One global curvature forces the same resolution everywhere, so prefix tokens smear across fan-out regimes and Stage 3 cannot separate "many possible next items" from "one likely next item".
NOVELTY: The curvature is neither a global constant nor a separate loss. Every codebook vector carries its own negative curvature computed from the measured successor-branching entropy of the training items currently assigned to that code, and that curvature enters the quantizer distance itself. Nothing in the repository ties per-code curvature to measured behaviour.
CHANGE: Replace d(z_i,e_k) in the RQ-VAE assignment with a code-specific hyperbolic distance d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k), where kappa_k is a deterministic, scale-relative function of the branching entropy H_k of code k, refreshed by EMA from training-only transitions. The decoder and reconstruction target are otherwise unchanged.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "u_i = exp_0^{k0}(z_i), k0 = -1 / median_i ||z_i||^2 (derived from encoder scale, not tuned). For every code k, p_kj = (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij + alpha) / (sum_j' (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij' + alpha)), alpha = 1, H_k = -sum_j p_kj log p_kj / log M, Hbar = mean_k H_k. kappa_k = k0 * exp(H_k - Hbar) clamped to [0.25*k0, 4*k0] (documented clamp, no sweep). Assignment logits l_ik = -d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 / tau with tau = median_{i,k} d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 computed once at epoch 0 and frozen. q_i = softmax(l_i). Loss = baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment; only assignment distances and code usage change. At each epoch end recompute hard a_i, accumulate T_ij from the training transition table restricted to items with a_i = k, and update H_k <- 0.9 H_k + 0.1 H_k^new; initialise H_k at global entropy. Freeze kappa_k after epoch 500 (documented warm-up, no tuning)."}
COST: One pass over the sparse training transition table per epoch: <= 24556 rows, ~O(10) stored successors each, < 0.5 s CPU per epoch, < 25 min over 3000 epochs, done once. Per step: same 1024 x 256 distance count plus one arcosh and one exp per logit, about 1.3x the quantizer cost and < 5% total step time.
HYPOTHESIS: If successor fan-out is heterogeneous and global curvature is a real bottleneck, codes in high-branching regions should acquire flatter effective metrics, per-code successor entropy of the top-1 next token should drop, and Stage 3 test Recall@10 should exceed 0.065 with no ablation arm trained. Observable in the per-code curvature histogram and Stage 3 prefix hit-rate.
RISKS: ['Entropy feedback can oscillate or collapse items into a few codes; the clamp and post-epoch-500 freeze are the guards. Per-code curvature makes dissimilarity asymmetric, so nearest-code search is no longer a metric nearest-neighbour problem; acceptable because codes are only compared as candidates. If branching entropy is nearly uniform, kappa_k is nearly constant and the mechanism reduces to baseline: safe failure but no gain.']
END IDEA

IDEA: SUCC-TAN-RQ
TITLE: Successor-directed tangent base shift for hyperbolic residual quantization
MOTIVATION: In residual quantization the second and third tokens encode whatever the first code failed to capture, in a direction unrelated to where users actually go next. When training transitions are directionally predictable, that predictability is spent on arbitrary residual bits instead of on a prefix a generative recommender can use.
NOVELTY: The residual chain is not reweighted and embeddings are not graph-smoothed. The quantizer's base point is transported along the measured mean successor-displacement tangent before the first code is chosen, and every later residual is taken in the tangent space of the chosen code; curvature controls the transport. This is a curved, behaviour-directed residual, distinct from behaviour-weighted distances or graph-regularised embeddings.
CHANGE: Before level 1, shift the item point along its measured successor direction in the tangent space at the origin: s_i = exp_0^k(log_0^k(u_i) + eta * t_i). Then quantize s_i with a hyperbolic residual quantizer whose level-l base is exp_{e_{c_l}}^k(xi_l) and whose codes are chosen by d_k(base, e_k). The reconstruction target remains the unshifted u_i, but the code chain is chosen to reconstruct s_i.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "t_i = (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} (log_0^k(u_j) - log_0^k(u_i)), S_i the training successors of i (out-degree capped at 32, most frequent). eta = d_code / (median_i ||t_i|| + 1e-8), d_code = median_{k != k'} d_k(e_k,e_k') measured at epoch 0; a typical successor shift then equals one code spacing, so eta is derived, not tuned. b_i^1 = s_i; c_1 = argmin_k d_k(b_i^1,e_k); xi_1 = log_{e_{c_1}}^k(b_i^1) - log_{e_{c_1}}^k(e_{c_1}); b_i^2 = exp_{e_{c_1}}^k(xi_1); c_2 = argmin_k d_k(b_i^2,e_k); and so on for L = 3 levels. u_hat_i = exp_0^k(sum_l log_0^k(e_{c_l})). L = d_k(u_i,u_hat_i)^2 + d_k(s_i,u_hat_i)^2 + commitment. The second term is the behaviour term, the first keeps item fidelity; both share u_hat, so behaviour changes the code chain that produces u_hat."}
COST: One extra exp/log per item per level and one successor-mean precomputation pass over training (~24556 items x <=32 successors) done once. Per step: 3 x 1024 x 256 distances with log/exp maps (~2x baseline quantizer arithmetic) plus two reconstruction terms; roughly 1.5x-2x baseline Stage 2 step time, no extra epochs or passes.
HYPOTHESIS: If transitions carry directional information that residuals currently destroy, shifting the base along the successor tangent should make true successor pairs share longer SID prefixes and raise Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observable as a rise in mean longest-common-prefix of held-out successor pairs and in Stage 3 recall at prefix lengths 1-3.
RISKS: ['The successor mean is noisy for tail items and can point uninformatively; the median-based eta keeps the shift at one code spacing but tail items may still be displaced too much. The shifted target can fight the reconstruction term and degrade item fidelity; sharing u_hat limits but does not remove this. Hyperbolic residual chains are numerically fragile near the ball boundary.']
END IDEA

IDEA: GEOPFX-SID
TITLE: Transition-pair geodesic alignment of hyperbolic prefix anchors
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender emits SID prefixes, so what matters is not only that related items are close but that the shared prefix lies "between" them along a path. Euclidean prefix codes have no betweenness: the shared prefix of two successor items can sit far off the line joining them, making the prefix a poor intermediate state for beam search.
NOVELTY: Behaviour does not weight the distance and is not a second loss. Each observed training transition selects a geodesic segment between two item SIDs, and the corresponding prefix anchor is pulled onto that segment in the Poincare ball. Curvature and behaviour meet inside one geometric residual, unlike a transition loss plus an unrelated hyperbolic regulariser.
CHANGE: Add one term per sampled training transition (i -> j): the squared hyperbolic distance from shared prefix anchor g_ij to the geodesic segment gamma(u_i,u_j), normalised by the pair's squared hyperbolic distance. The anchor is the exp-map of the sum of the shared prefix code logs.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'LCP_ij = number of leading SID tokens equal for i and j. g_ij = exp_0^k(sum_{m <= LCP_ij} log_0^k(e_{c_m(i)})); if LCP = 0 the pair is skipped (documented default: no shared prefix to align). gamma(u_i,u_j)(s) = exp_{u_i}^k(s * Pi_{u_i}(log_{u_i}^k(u_j))), s in [0,1]. delta(g,gamma) = min_s d_k(g,gamma(s)) via 12 golden-section steps on [0,1]. L_geo = (1/|E_b|) sum_{(i,j) in E_b} w_ij * delta^2 / (d_k(u_i,u_j)^2 + eps), w_ij = transition count, eps = 1e-6, term weight fixed at 1 (documented default). E_b is a uniform sample of at most 2048 training transitions per step. Total loss = baseline RQ-VAE loss + L_geo. No other change to the quantizer.'}
COST: 2048 pairs x 12 golden-section evaluations x one Poincare distance each per step, about 24.5k extra distances versus 1024 x 256 = 262k quantizer distances, so ~+10% quantizer work and well under +10% total step time. Transition list precomputed once; sampling O(2048) per step; 72,000 steps total.
HYPOTHESIS: If prefix tokens are intermediate beam states in Stage 3, moving the shared anchor onto the geometric path between successor items should make true successors share prefixes more often and make those prefixes more predictive. Observable as an increase in area under the prefix hit-rate curve and Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: ['At the start no two items share a prefix, so LCP = 0 for almost all pairs and the term is inert until codes agree; warm-up and a minimum-LCP filter help but may make the term arrive late. The geodesic minimum can be flat when g is already close to the segment, giving weak gradients. Optimising this term can distort item-level reconstruction if weight 1 is too strong relative to the baseline loss.']
END IDEA

IDEA: GEO-SHELL-RQ
TITLE: Codebook atoms placed on radial shells whose radius is the measured branching of the training transition tree.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE spreads every level's codebook over the same latent volume, so a coarse prefix covering a huge behavioural subtree occupies no more room than a leaf covering three items. The generator then has to memorise which of 256 equally sized prefixes is broad, which is exactly the prefix behaviour predictability Stage 3 struggles with.
NOVELTY: The behaviour statistic sets the RADIUS of each individual atom inside the curved ball, i.e. the atom positions, not the assignment weight and not a loss. The radius is a closed-form tree-embedding quantity, so nothing is tuned.
CHANGE: Each atom is an anchor plus a small learnable tangent offset; the anchor is the Frechet-mean direction of its training-interaction community placed at the hyperbolic radius implied by that community's measured leaf mass, and every step atoms are geodesically projected back into their shell.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Symmetrise training transition counts A = C + C^T; build an L-level community tree (recursive Leiden / normalised cut) with N level-L leaves; for level-l community g, B_g = measured number of leaf descendants; r_lg = (N - B_g)/(N + B_g); rho_lg = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) r_lg); u_hat = unit direction of the Frechet mean of the frozen item content embeddings in g; m = exp_0(rho_lg u_hat); e = exp_m(eps); forward RQ identical to the baseline except that distances are d_c; after each optimiser step project e along the geodesic diameter onto [rho_lg - delta, rho_lg + delta].'}
COST: One-off tree construction and Frechet precompute over 24556 items on CPU (minutes, before training). Per step only the O(K L d) = 256*3*64 ~ 5e4 elementwise projection plus the d_c terms already computed for assignment, well under 1% of Stage-2 wall clock, and zero marginal Stage-3 cost.
HYPOTHESIS: If the ball radius given to a prefix should match how many leaves it must separate, broad behaviour communities will occupy large-radius shells and their token will become predictable from a short history; prefix-conditional accuracy rises and Stage-3 recall@10 clears 0.065.
RISKS: ['The community tree may disagree with the content geometry and put anchor directions in the wrong cones; hard shell projection can freeze atoms; the Sarkar radius saturates near 1 for huge subtrees and loses radial resolution exactly where branching is largest.']
END IDEA

IDEA: GYRO-TARGET-RQ
TITLE: The autoencoder reconstructs a geodesic-shifted successor barycentre instead of the item itself.
MOTIVATION: Many items are interchangeable given the same successor distribution; giving each its own code wastes generator capacity on distinctions the behaviour does not make. What the next-item predictor needs is the item's behavioural role, not its identity.
NOVELTY: The behaviour signal changes the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET inside the curved ball. It is not an extra loss term, not a reweighted assignment and not a codebook prior, so the coupling cannot be removed by dropping a regulariser.
CHANGE: The reconstruction target of item i is a point on the geodesic from its own ball point toward the hyperbolic mean of its training successors, displaced by a fraction fixed by the item's measured transition concentration.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'S_i = immediate next items of i in training sessions; c_i = max_j p(i->j); eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i) in [0,1/2]; b_i = exp_{p_i}( eta_i * (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} log_{p_i}(sg(p_j)) ); loss = d_c(phat_i, b_i)^2 + commitment; successor points p_j come from a stop-gradient table refreshed once per epoch.'}
COST: Successor table refresh is O(E d) once per epoch (E ~ 1e5 edges, d = 64, ~6e6 flops, amortised to ~2.5e5 flops per step) plus one extra exp/log pair per item, O(B d), against the existing encoder step. Negligible in Stage 2, a few MB of CSR storage, Stage 3 unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: If SIDs encode behavioural role, items with the same successor set collapse onto one code and the generator's next-prefix prediction becomes easier; observed as fewer distinct codes per successor-set cluster, higher prefix conditional accuracy, and Stage-3 recall@10 above 0.065.
RISKS: ['Over-smoothing can merge genuinely distinct items and collapse recall; the momentum table can lag and create a moving target early in training; c_i is noisy for rare items and can over-shift them.']
END IDEA

IDEA: KAPPA_BRANCH
TITLE: Training-branching sets a per-item curvature field that drives the RQ-VAE assignment metric.
MOTIVATION: A content-only RQ-VAE gives every item the same geometric room. Items with many behaviourally distinct successors (broad-appeal hubs) get coarse prefixes that cannot separate those successors, while leaf items waste capacity. In a negatively curved space volume grows exponentially with radius, so the place where the training transition graph branches is exactly where more negative curvature buys separation per bit; where it does not branch, extra curvature only adds distortion.
NOVELTY: Curvature is neither a global hyperparameter nor a trainable scalar. It is a per-item field computed from the training-only transition graph and injected into the pair distance used for nearest-code search, codebook gradient and hence SID assignment. Existing behaviour-aware quantizers reweight the data term of a Euclidean quantizer; here behaviour changes the metric itself, and the metric changes the codes.
CHANGE: Each item gets kappa_i from its normalised successor branch entropy; the RQ-VAE assigns and commits with a symmetrised Poincare distance whose curvature is the harmonic mean of the two endpoints' curvatures, so codebook gradients, code occupancy and the final SID all move with the training graph.

IDEA: GEO_REPAIR
TITLE: Behaviour-directed geodesic reassignment of colliding semantic IDs so the generator's reachable item set stops depending on arbitrary tie-breaks.
MOTIVATION: The quantizer maps many items onto the same three-token SID; the generator can only emit one item per SID, so the rest become effectively unreachable and recall is capped by an arbitrary content tie-break that has nothing to do with what users actually do next. Adding codes or a fourth level changes the vocabulary and the Stage-3 protocol; nothing has to change if the ambiguous tail of the assignment is decided by behaviour instead.
NOVELTY: The curved operation acts on the decision rule for already-ambiguous items only, not on the encoder, the loss or a global assignment. The behaviour centroid is the reference point, the Poincare distance to the candidate codes is the criterion, and the representative of each collision class is chosen by training in-degree, so the SID the generator already emits stays fixed and only the unreachable duplicates are moved to where their successors say they belong.
CHANGE: After the epoch's assignment, group items by full SID; the highest training in-degree item keeps the ID, and every other member is re-assigned at the last level (or the second level if the parent prefix has no free code) to the code geodesically closest to its training successor centroid.

IDEA: LORENTZ_CONE_RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-weighted Lorentz future-cone ordering inside geodesic residual quantisation
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built by residual reconstruction error alone, so a level-2 prefix is chosen because it reduces distortion, not because the item actually follows the level-1 item in user behaviour. A generative next-item model then has to rediscover transition direction from a prefix code that has already discarded it, and every extra level of RQ depth adds a distortion-driven split that cuts across real user trajectories.

It makes the SID codebook a partially ordered object: consecutive-level centroids are put under a Lorentz causal-cone order whose strength is the training-only directed transition mass between the corresponding code pairs, and the same centroids serve as the base and target of the log/exp residual step. Removing the behaviour term or the curvature term changes the centroid geometry and therefore the emitted SID prefixes, not merely an auxiliary loss.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean residual quantiser with a Lorentz geodesic residual quantiser (log map at the parent centroid, nearest tangent codebook, exp map back), and add a transition-mass-weighted future-cone hinge on the same per-level centroids at every optimiser step, so codebook geometry is jointly shaped by reconstruction and by measured transition order.

A point y is in the future cone of x iff <y-x, y-x>_L <= 0 and (y0 - x0) > 0. Build M_l once from the Stage-2 training split. At each residual level l = 1..3, the code is q_l = argmin_k || log_{e_{l-1}}(x_{l-1}) - T_l[k] ||^2 and the level output is x_l = exp_{e_{l-1}}(T_l[q_l]) with e_0 = origin. COST: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps) the transition matrix is built in one pass over training transitions before training, under 60 s and about 0.1% of the run. Per step the extra work is about 3 levels x 2048 sampled transition pairs = roughly 6k hinge evaluations plus a 256x256 gather and one additional aggregation pass for the geodesic Fréchet-style centroid update; estimated +3 to +6% step time, and 0.8M floats of memory for three 256x256 matrices. No extra epochs and no extra forward passes.
HYPOTHESIS: If transition direction is information the prefix should carry, then forcing frequent successor codes into the future cone of their parent code will lower the cone-violation rate and raise the accuracy with which the level-2 code is predicted from the level-1 code, and the Stage-3 generative model will convert that into test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run.
